title: Punjab's shared devotional ground
hook: a queen left alone at the forest's edge, and the poet who finds her

segments.voice: Yesterday, Punjab's shared devotional ground: Vaisakhi, one spring day, each neighbor keeping its own meaning.
screen: `THE SAME DAY, EACH ITS OWN MEANING.`

segments.voice: A woman sits alone at the edge of a forest, crying. She is Sita, the queen of Ayodhya, and she's carrying a child. Ram has sent her away because of what people in the city were saying, and the brother who drove her here has gone back. Young students from a nearby hermitage hear her and run to tell their teacher. He comes out to her. He's Valmiki, the poet of the Ramayana, and he finds the heroine of his own story weeping at his door. Today, Punjab's last stop: a place tradition calls that door.
screen: `SITA ALONE AT THE FOREST'S EDGE.` → `THE STUDENTS RUN FOR THEIR TEACHER.` → `VALMIKI COMES OUT.`

segments.voice: In the last book of Valmiki's Ramayana, in paraphrase, Valmiki speaks gently to Sita. He tells her he knows she has done no wrong. He brings her into his hermitage and gives her into the care of the women there, to be looked after like a daughter. First, the shelter. The poet who tells the whole story of Ram also shelters Sita when the story turns hard on her. Her twin sons, Lava and Kusha, are born there and grow up in the hermitage. Valmiki teaches them the Ramayana, and in the story they sing it, their own father's story, before Ram himself. Then, the place. Tradition places Valmiki's hermitage at Ram Tirath, near Amritsar. There's a temple and a sacred tank, and pilgrims come to the place where, the story says, Sita found shelter and her sons were born. Last, who honors him. Tradition calls Valmiki the first poet, the adi kavi. In Punjab, the Valmiki community honors him with special devotion as Bhagwan Valmiki, and his birthday is kept with processions. Each comes to him in its own way, and the place holds them all. And that's where the regional journey ends: Tamil hymns, Bengal's streams, the Varkari road, Kashmir, Kerala's Onam and Ayyappa, Gujarat's courtyard of questions, and Punjab, where songs, festivals and holy places are held as shared ground. Tomorrow, before the festivals that close the year, the path stops and sits at the top of the climb.
screen: `VALMIKI SHELTERS SITA` · `THE TWINS LEARN THE RAMAYANA` · `RAM TIRATH, NEAR AMRITSAR` · `HONORED BY EACH IN ITS OWN WAY`

segments.voice: Think of a time when life turned hard and someone took you in: a friend's couch, a teacher's office, a grandparent's kitchen, a kind word at the right moment. Let that person come to mind, feel what it was like to be sheltered, and for a few breaths simply wish them well; if you pray, hold them before God. If life feels that hard right now, you don't have to carry it alone: in the US you can call or text 988, or call local emergency help.
